newsitem.title: UK: C&W active, analysts upgrade forecasts.
newsitem.headline: C&W active, analysts upgrade forecasts.

text.p: Shares in Cable & Wireless were actively traded on Thursday as industry analysts upgraded their profit forecasts following news that energy giant RWE had joined its German alliance.
The shares were one of the most actively traded stocks with over six million changing hands before midday. The price was unchanged at 430p.
Most analysts said they remain buyers of the stock and have reiterated this stance after revising profit forecasts in the UK telecoms group upwards on the alliance news.
Jim McCafferty at ABN Amro Hoare Govett added 50 million stg to his forecasts for 1998 and 1999 and repeated his positive stance on the shares.
"The formation of this new alliance significantly improves the company's financial position through reduced start-up losses, improved cashflow and reduced gearing," he said.
Gearing for the group stood at 1.32 in March this year.

An article in the Financial Times today criticised the C&W strategy of heavy investment in basic insfrastructure, preferring instead British Telecom's approach to creating one network capable of carrying both mobile and fixed calls.

"It's going to take a long time before an interconnector agreement is established in Germany," McCafferty said, referring to BT's strategy. "If you want to be a service provider, by the time you get into the market the less there will be," he added. But Laurence Heyworth, analyst at Robert Fleming Securities disagreed and said that despite a likely adjustment to his forecasts, they will remain sellers of Cable & Wireless shares. "There is considerable merit to the BT approach," Heyworth said.
